# Incident Report: Information-Stealer Infection — SPOONWATCH.NET Domain

**Evidence reviewed:** `2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,880 frames, capture window 2022-01-07 20:04:09–20:16:40 +0400). No supplementary IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence folder; findings below are derived directly from the pcap using tshark.

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **192.168.1.216** | DHCP ACK, all sessions |
| MAC address | **9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9** (ASUSTek Computer Inc. NIC) | ARP/Ethernet source on all frames from .216 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** | DHCP Option 12 (hostname), NBNS name registration, mDNS/LLMNR queries |
| AD domain | SPOONWATCH.NET (DC: SPOONWATCH-DC, 192.168.1.2) | DNS SRV lookups for `_ldap._tcp...spoonwatch.net`, NBNS |
| Logged-in Windows user | **steve.smith** | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ `CNameString` = `steve.smith` (frames to/from 192.168.1.2:88), machine account `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$` also authenticating separately |

## 2. Malware Family

**Vidar Stealer (Oski-lineage information-stealer).** Attribution is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed** — no AV/YARA match was performed (no internet lookup used, per instructions). The behavioral fingerprint is strong and internally consistent:

- All C2 requests carry `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8` and **no `User-Agent` header** — a distinctive HTTP client fingerprint associated with Vidar/Arkei-family stealer bots.
- The bot first fetches a sequence of files named `1.jpg` through `7.jpg` from its C2 panel. Despite the `.jpg` name and `Content-Type: image/jpeg` in the response, every one of these is actually a **Windows PE32 DLL** (confirmed via `file` and internal strings): legitimate Mozilla NSS/SQLite components (`freebl`, Mozilla NSS/mozglue symbols, `sqlite_master` engine) and Microsoft VC++ runtime libraries (`MSVCP140.dll`, `VCRUNTIME140.dll`, `CONCRT140.dll`). This is the classic Vidar technique of pulling down the exact third-party DLLs (NSS3/SQLite3/VC redist) it needs to open and decrypt Chrome/Firefox/Edge profile databases.
- The stealer then POSTs its loot as a single ZIP (`_5861695120.zip`) to the C2 panel path `/osk/`, whose internal folder layout — `autofill/`, `cookies/`, `cc/`, each containing per-browser files such as `Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `Google Chrome_Network.txt` — matches the Vidar/Oski output schema for stolen autofill data, cookies, and credit-card form data.
- The panel path itself (`/osk/…`) is the Oski-stealer naming convention that Vidar's codebase inherited.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

**Command-and-control:**
- `2.56.57.108:80` (TCP/HTTP) — sole C2 endpoint. Contacted by hardcoded IP with **no preceding DNS lookup**; this is the only external, non-Microsoft endpoint the host communicates with (all other DNS/TLS traffic resolves to legitimate `*.microsoft.com`, `*.windowsupdate.com`, `bing.com`, `msn.com` infrastructure).

**Malicious domains:** None — the C2 is contacted purely by IP literal, no domain observed for it in DNS traffic.

**Malicious URLs (HTTP, plaintext):**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `http://2.56.57.108/osk//7.jpg` — GET responses deliver DLL payloads disguised as images
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` — check-in
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` — POST, exfiltration of stolen-data archive (Content-Length 379,629 bytes)

**Transferred files and SHA-256 hashes (extracted from HTTP objects in the pcap):**

| File (as named in traffic) | Role | Size | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_5861695120.zip` | Exfiltrated stolen-data archive (autofill/cookies/cc) | 379,629 B | `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f` |
| `1.jpg` (actual: SQLite-engine DLL) | Downloaded helper module | 645,592 B | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` |
| `2.jpg` (actual: Mozilla NSS/freebl DLL) | Downloaded helper module | 334,288 B | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` |
| `3.jpg` (actual: Mozilla NSS DLL) | Downloaded helper module | 137,168 B | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` |
| `4.jpg` (actual: MSVCP140/VCRUNTIME140 DLL) | Downloaded helper module | 440,120 B | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` |
| `5.jpg` (actual: SQLite-engine DLL) | Downloaded helper module | 1,246,160 B | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` |
| `6.jpg` (actual: Mozilla NSS/freebl DLL) | Downloaded helper module | 144,848 B | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083` |
| `7.jpg` (actual: VCRUNTIME140 DLL) | Downloaded helper module | 83,784 B | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` |

**Not malicious (verified benign, ruled out during analysis):** the `au.download.windowsupdate.com` / `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` `.cab`/`.exe` downloads from Akamai-fronted Microsoft IPs (23.38.189.201/225, 8.253.189.126) are legitimate Windows Defender/Windows Update traffic, correctly resolved via DNS and delivered over standard Microsoft CDN infrastructure.

## 4. Summary

Host **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), logged in as domain user **steve.smith** on the **SPOONWATCH.NET** domain, is compromised by a **Vidar-family information stealer**. The malware beaconed to **2.56.57.108:80**, pulled down legitimate browser-crypto/runtime DLLs disguised as JPEGs to enable credential/cookie decryption, and exfiltrated a ZIP archive of stolen Chrome/Edge autofill, cookie, and payment-card data to the same host over plaintext HTTP.
